report:
**Conclusion:** Contrary to your initial expectation, clinical evidence indicates that olive leaf extract **can** help lower elevated blood pressure, particularly in individuals with prehypertension or stage-1 hypertension.

### Summary of Evidence

* **Efficacy Comparable to Prescription Medication:** A double-blind randomized controlled trial in patients with stage-1 hypertension evaluated taking 500 mg of olive leaf extract twice daily against Captopril (a standard ACE inhibitor medication). After eight weeks, olive leaf extract significantly reduced both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, demonstrating effectiveness comparable to Captopril (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21036583/, https://naturalhealthresearch.org/olive-leaf-lowers-blood-pressure/).
* **Mechanism of Action:** The primary bioactive compound in olive leaf extract is **oleuropein**. Research shows oleuropein acts as a vasodilator, antioxidant, and natural ACE inhibitor, helping relax blood vessels and improve vascular flow.
* **Clinical Trial Findings:** Other clinical studies, including an eight-week trial using 1,000 mg daily of olive leaf extract, recorded statistically significant drops in both blood pressure readings and LDL cholesterol in adults with borderline high blood pressure (https://www.birthandbeyondmagazine.com/wellness-features-blog/2015/2/11/blueberries-could-lower-your-blood-pressure-rct-data, https://www.irishtimes.com/news/health/does-it-work-1.613554).

While clinical evidence supports its efficacy for mild hypertension, individuals taking prescription antihypertensives should consult a physician before using olive leaf extract to avoid excessive blood pressure drops or drug interactions.
